name: Label dose against the Ayurvedic Formulary of India
description: For classical preparations where the Ayurvedic Formulary of India states a dose, what each manufacturer states on its own product page, and how the two relate. Every row carries the manufacturer's own words and the URL they were read from.
method: Label text was collected deterministically from each manufacturer's own product page. The comparison itself was judged by a model, one pass per preparation, and every comparable verdict was then re-checked by a second adversarial pass that defaults to refusing. A claim is published only where that second pass named it confirmed. Two of 62 were withheld.
limits: This states the relation between two published figures and nothing else. It is not a safety assessment and not a finding that any dose is wrong. A manufacturer may differ from the formulary for legitimate reasons including preparation strength and indication. Where the formulary figure is the weight of drug used to prepare a decoction rather than the amount swallowed, no comparison is drawn.

withheld.why: The file holds two Maharishi Ayurveda pages with conflicting doses: the 50 ml page says 'Take 3 to 12 ml Twice a day', the other says '1-2 teaspoon daily after meals' (roughly 5 to 10 ml once daily). The claim reports only the first as the brand's dose and ignores the second. Separately, the relation 'overlapping' rests on a single shared endpoint: [3, 12] and the formulary's [12, 24] meet only at 12 ml, so the Maharishi range sits at or below the formulary minimum rather than genuinely overlapping it. Population is unstated on both pages; note that 3 to 12 ml is exactly the range Kerala Ayurveda labels as the children's dose, so treating it as an adult figure is unsupported by the raw text.
withheld.correction: Either publish both Maharishi figures (3 to 12 ml twice a day on one page; 1 to 2 teaspoon daily on another) with the relation described as 'at or below the formulary minimum, touching 12 ml', or drop the brand from the comparison until a single authoritative label is settled.

withheld.why: The label states a DAILY amount ("Take 3 to 6 grams daily"), while the formulary figure (AFI Part I 7:34, "1 to 3 g") is a per-dose weight of powder. The relation "overlapping" is only reached by treating the daily total as a single-administration dose; if the 3 to 6 g is divided across the day (as churna doses normally are), the per-dose amount falls within 1 to 3 g, which would change the relation. Additionally, 3-6 g and 1-3 g share only the single endpoint 3 g, which is boundary contact rather than an overlapping range. Digits (3, 6) and the quote are correctly transcribed from the raw text; the fault is the frequency basis and the relation label, not the number.
withheld.correction: Report the Maharishi figure as "3 to 6 g daily (frequency unstated)" and do not assign a relation against the per-dose formulary figure; if a relation must be given, state that the daily total of 3 to 6 g equals a per-dose range of 1.5 to 3 g if taken twice daily (within the formulary range) or 3 to 6 g if taken once daily (touching the upper bound at 3 g), and that the label does not say which.
